posts.topic: Pattern symbols: grainline, place on fold, notches

slides.title: 3 pattern symbols every beginner should know
slides.subtitle: Read these right and your garment hangs, matches and fits the way it was designed to.

slides.title: The grainline
slides.body: This long double arrow must run parallel to the selvedge. Measure from both ends of the arrow to the edge of the fabric: when the two numbers match, pin it down.

slides.title: Place on fold
slides.body: A bracket with arrows means this edge goes exactly on the folded edge of your fabric. Don't cut along it: you'll get one symmetrical piece twice as wide.

slides.title: Notches
slides.body: These little triangles are matching points. Snip them into the seam allowance (never past it), then line them up when you sew so the pieces join perfectly.

slides.title: Save this for your next project
slides.body: Every Pattern Perfection pattern explains its symbols step by step, so you never have to guess.

slides.title: Always pre-wash your fabric before you cut
slides.body: Cotton, linen and viscose can shrink after the first wash. Wash and dry your fabric the same way you'll care for the finished garment, then press it and cut. Your perfect fit stays perfect.

posts.caption_ig:
The sewing tip nobody tells you until it's too late: pre-wash your fabric 🧺

Natural fibres like cotton, linen and viscose can shrink in the first wash. Sew first, wash later, and your perfectly fitted garment can come out a size smaller.

Wash and dry it exactly how you'll care for the finished piece, press, then cut ✂️

Do you always pre-wash? Be honest 😅

posts.topic: Choosing your size XS-XL with US/UK sizing

slides.title: How to choose your pattern size (XS–XL)
slides.subtitle: Spoiler: it's probably not the size you buy in shops. Here's how to get it right first time.

slides.title: Measure, don't guess
slides.body: Wear thin clothes and measure your full bust, natural waist and fullest hip, keeping the tape level and snug but not tight. Write the numbers down.

slides.title: Compare with the size chart
slides.body: Use the size chart on the pattern, not your ready-to-wear size. Ours follow US and UK standards from XS to XL, so you can compare your numbers directly.

slides.title: Between sizes? Blend them
slides.body: Choose tops by bust and skirts by hip. If you sit between sizes, draw a smooth line from one size to the other at the waist. It's called grading, and it's easy.

slides.title: Find your perfect fit
slides.body: Every pattern includes sizes XS–XL with US and UK sizing and a clear size chart.
